key_insight: A local measurement-and-feedforward routing protocol can generate scalable graph states with amortized O(1) decision delay, keeping classical latency well below qubit coherence limits.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical routing strategy for quantum networks that prioritizes time-feasible entanglement generation and supports modular construction of larger distributed quantum computing states.
method: Use local measurements plus classical feedforward instead of global state computation
Map the protocol to a dual-species trapped-ion network architecture
Apply hybrid simulation and noise analysis, with erasure transformation and spatial multiplexing to improve robustness
evidence_signal: Hybrid simulations and noise analysis indicate the protocol is resource-efficient and time-feasible, with readout fidelity identified as the main performance bottleneck.
watch_item: The approach is highly sensitive to readout errors, so practical deployment will depend on effective noise suppression and reliable branching independence in hardware.
paper_title: Scalable Graph State Generation with O(1) Local Feedforward in Quantum Networks
